newsitem.title: USA: CME plans smaller Eurodollar ticks from March 3.
newsitem.headline: CME plans smaller Eurodollar ticks from March 3.

text.p: The Chicago Mercantile Exchange plans to start trading March 3 in smaller minimum price increments on interest rate futures contracts, the exchange said Friday.

Pending approval by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, the CME plans half-tick trading on the serial and first through fourth quarterly Eurodollar futures and options, and on all LIBOR and T-bill futures and options.
The CME also plans to implement quarter-tick trading in all Eurodollar "pack" combinations on March 3.
The exchange's board of directors approved the implementation schedule Wednesday.
Until recently, all CME interest rate futures were quoted in full basis points, or increments of 0.01 each worth $25.00.
The CME has already tested half-ticks, or 0.005 basis point, each worth $12.50, with some expiring Eurodollar futures during their delivery months.
The CME at a February 5 board meeting also planned a second phase of changes to take effect, pending regulatory approval and further review by the board, 60 days after the first set of changes.

The second phase would include a further cut in the minimum price move to quarter-ticks, or 0.0025 basis point worth $6.25 each, in the serial and nearest March quarterly Eurodollar futures and options.
At the same time, the CME plans to move to half-tick trading in Eurodollar "red" contract months (fifth through eighth quarterly contracts).
Also in the second phase, it plans quarter-tick trading for LIBOR and T-bill futures and options and Federal funds futures, comparable to their Eurodollar counterparts.
The CME had originally planned to include the move to quarter-ticks in Eurodollar "pack" combinations in the second phase, but the board decided on Wednesday to advance this change to March 3.

"Packs" are four consecutive quarterly contracts for a one-year period within a "color" that are bought or sold at the same time. "Color" contracts are assigned color codes based on the time to termination in terms of years. Red is assigned to the second group of four quarterly contracts, which is currently March through December 1998. ((Derivatives Desk (312) 408-8750)) ((E-mail: derivatives@reuters.com))
